Latin

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈɫuːk.soː], [ˈɫʊk.soː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈluk.so]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From lūxus (“dislocated”). Cognate with Ancient Greek λοξός (loxós, “slanting”).

Verb

[edit]

lū̆xō (present infinitive lū̆xāre, perfect active lū̆xāvī, supine lū̆xātum); first conjugation

  1. to put out of joint, dislocate
  2. to displace

[edit]

  1. dative/ablative masculine/neuter singular of lū̆xus

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Latin luxus (“extravagance, luxury”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈlu.ʃu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈlu.ʃu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈlu.ʃo/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈlu.ʃu/

  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -uʃu
  • Hyphenation: lu‧xo

Noun

[edit]

luxo m (plural luxos)

  1. (uncountable) extravagance; prodigality
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:luxo
  2. luxury (something pleasant but unnecessary)
    Synonym: excesso
Antonyms
[edit]
  • (antonym(s) of “extravagance”): see Thesaurus:luxo
Derived terms
[edit]
  • cheio de luxo
  • dar ao luxo de

[edit]

  • luxento
  • luxuosidade
  • luxuoso
  • luxúria
  • luxuriar
  • luxurioso

[edit]

Verb
